title: The DG homotopy category and its acyclic Verdier class
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. A differential graded algebra over $\mathbf Z$ means an associative unital graded ring $A=\bigoplus_{i\in\mathbf Z}A^i$ with additive differential $d:A^i\to A^{i+1}$ satisfying $d^2=0$ and $d(ab)=d(a)b+(-1)^ia\,d(b)$ for $a\in A^i$. A right differential graded $A$-module is a graded right module $M$ with $d^2=0$ and $d(ma)=d(m)a+(-1)^jm\,d(a)$ for $m\in M^j$. Let $K(A,d)$ be the category of right DG $A$-modules with degree-zero $A$-linear chain maps modulo homotopy: $f\sim g$ if $f-g=d_Nh+hd_M$ for a degree-$-1$ right $A$-linear map $h:M\to N$. Use shifts $M[k]^i=M^{i+k}$ with differential $(-1)^kd_M$ and unchanged right action. For a chain map $f:M\to N$, set $C(f)^i=N^i\oplus M^{i+1}$ with differential $d(y,x)=(d_Ny+f(x),-d_Mx)$ and componentwise right action. Declare triangles distinguished when they are isomorphic in $K(A,d)$ to a cone triangle $M\xrightarrow{f}N\xrightarrow{i}C(f)\xrightarrow{-p}M[1]$, where $i(y)=(y,0)$ and $p(y,x)=x$, so that the third map sends $(y,x)$ to $-x$. Let $\mathcal E$ be the full subcategory on acyclic modules, meaning $H^i(M)=\ker(d_M:M^i\to M^{i+1})/d_M(M^{i-1})=0$ for every integer $i$. Then $K(A,d)$ is a triangulated category [def-weil-triangulated-category], and $\mathcal E$ is a strictly full triangulated subcategory [def-weil-triangulated-subcategory]. The class $W_{\mathcal E}$ of morphisms $u:X\to Y$ admitting a distinguished triangle $X\xrightarrow{u}Y\to Z\to X[1]$ with $Z\in\mathcal E$ is exactly the class of morphisms inducing isomorphisms on every $H^i$. No boundedness or commutativity hypothesis on $A$ or the modules is imposed.

source.place: Tag 09KJ, proposition-homotopy-category-triangulated; Tag 09KW, lemma-acyclic, including its identification of the associated cone multiplicative system with quasi-isomorphisms.

proof.text: Write $K_A=K(A,d)$ and $T_f=(X,Y,C(f),f,i_f,-p_f)$. Homotopy is an additive congruence: sums and negatives of homotopies remain homotopies, and composing $h$ with chain maps $a,b$ gives the homotopy $bha$. Hence the quotient has abelian Hom groups and bilinear composition. The zero module and componentwise finite direct sums retain their zero and biproduct identities in the quotient. Shifts preserve the DG rule: for $m\in M[k]^n$, $(-1)^kd_M(ma)=(-1)^kd_M(m)a+(-1)^nm\,d_A(a)$. They send a homotopy $h$ to $(-1)^kh$, are additive, and satisfy $[k][l]=[k+l]$. For the cone, $d_C^2(y,x)=(d_Yf(x)-fd_X(x),0)=0$; in its second coordinate $-d_X(xa)=(-d_Xx)a+(-1)^nx\,d_A(a)$ for $x\in X^{n+1}$, and the first coordinate has the same DG rule. Thus the stated cones and their maps exist. Every quotient morphism has a chain representative and hence a cone triangle. Moreover $C(1_X)$ contracts by $h(y,x)=(0,y)$, since $dh+hd=1$, so $T_{1_X}$ is isomorphic via $(1,1,0)$ to $(X,X,0,1,0,0)$. Together with isomorphism closure by definition, these are the additive, shift and TR1 requirements of [def-weil-triangulated-category].

source.place: Definitions of homotopy, shift and cone; Tag 09KH, lemma-homotopy-category-pre-triangulated, TR1; signed convention of Tag 09KF.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-dg-cone-rotation] to each chain map $f$. It identifies both the rotation of $T_f$ and its inverse rotation with standard cone triangles, with exactly the negative projection and the rotated last arrow $-f[1]$. Rotating a triangle isomorphism is again a triangle isomorphism. Therefore both rotation and inverse rotation preserve the class declared distinguished, proving TR2.

source.place: Tags 09KB and 09KC, lemma-rotate-cone and lemma-rotate-triangle; Tag 09KH, TR2.

proof.text: For TR3, choose isomorphisms putting both distinguished triangles in standard cone form $T_f,T_{f'}$, and conjugate the specified first square by their first two components. Represent its two maps by chain maps $a:X\to X'$, $b:Y\to Y'$. Commutativity in $K_A$ supplies a degree-$-1$ $A$-linear $h$ with $bf-f'a=d_{Y'}h+hd_X$. Define $c:C(f)\to C(f')$ by $c(y,x)=(by+hx,ax)$. Its upper-right chain-map equation is $d_{Y'}h+f'a=bf-hd_X$, exactly that homotopy equation; the other entries use that $a,b$ are chain maps. It is $A$-linear and satisfies $ci_f=i_{f'}b$ and $(-p_{f'})c=a[1](-p_f)$. Undoing the chosen triangle isomorphisms gives TR3. Together with steps 1 and 2 this makes $K_A$ pre-triangulated.

source.place: Tag 09KD, lemma-functorial-cone, explicit matrix with homotopy bf-f′a; Tag 09KH, TR3.

proof.text: For composable representatives $f:X\to Y$, $g:Y\to Z$, apply [lem-sfb-dg-composite-cone-contraction]. Its maps $\alpha(y,x)=(gy,x)$, $\beta(z,x)=(z,fx)$ and $\gamma(z,y)=(-y,0)$ give a triangle on $C(f),C(gf),C(g)$ isomorphic to $T_\alpha$, hence distinguished. The four octahedral squares hold on representatives: $\alpha i_f=i_{gf}g$, $(-p_{gf})\alpha=-p_f$, $\beta i_{gf}=i_g$, and $(-p_g)\beta=f[1](-p_{gf})$. The final arrow is precisely $\gamma=i_f[1](-p_g)$. This gives the octahedron required in [def-weil-triangulated-category] for the three standard cone triangles.

source.place: Tag 09KI, lemma-two-split-injections, in cone coordinates; Tag 09KJ, proposition-homotopy-category-triangulated, TR4.

proof.text: Now take any three prescribed distinguished triangles with first arrows $[f],[g],[gf]$. By TR3 already proved, the identity square on the first two objects extends from each standard cone triangle to the corresponding prescribed triangle. By [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso], valid for a pre-triangulated category, each third component is an isomorphism. If these are $c_f,c_g,c_{gf}$, replace $\alpha,\beta,\gamma$ by $c_{gf}\alpha c_f^{-1}$, $c_g\beta c_{gf}^{-1}$, $c_f[1]\gamma c_g^{-1}$. The triangle equations for the $c$'s substitute into the four equalities of step 4, and its final-arrow equality becomes the composite of the prescribed arrow to $Y[1]$ with the prescribed arrow from $Y[1]$. The fourth triangle remains distinguished by isomorphism closure. Thus TR4 holds for arbitrary prescribed triangles and $K_A$ is triangulated.

source.place: Tag 09KJ, arbitrary-cone reduction; derived.tex Tag 014A, lemma-third-isomorphism-triangle, and Tag 014C, lemma-easier-axiom-four.

proof.text: Cohomology is well-defined on $K_A$: if $f-g=dh+hd$ and $x$ is a cycle, then $(f-g)x=d(hx)$, so $H^n(f)=H^n(g)$. Identity and composition on cycles descend to identity and composition on their quotients, so every $H^n$ is a functor and preserves isomorphisms. For a shift, kernels are unchanged and images are unchanged because multiplication by $(-1)^k$ is invertible; hence $H^n(M[k])=H^{n+k}(M)$ under the underlying-group identification.

source.place: Tag 09KW, lemma-acyclic, underlying cohomology functors; definitions of homotopy and shift.

proof.text: We verify the cone criterion directly. Suppose all $H^n(f)$ are bijective. For a degree-$n$ cycle $(y,x)$ in $C(f)$, $d_Xx=0$ and $d_Yy=-fx$. Injectivity of $H^{n+1}(f)$ gives $x=d_Xt$ for $t\in X^n$. Then $y+ft$ is closed; surjectivity of $H^n(f)$ gives a cycle $z\in X^n$ and $w\in Y^{n-1}$ with $y+ft=fz+d_Yw$. Consequently $(y,x)=d_C(w,z-t)$, proving acyclicity. Conversely suppose $C(f)$ acyclic. A cycle $y\in Y^n$ gives a cone cycle $(y,0)$, so $(y,0)=d_C(w,t)$ for $w\in Y^{n-1},t\in X^n$; then $d_Xt=0$ and $y=d_Yw+ft$, proving surjectivity of $H^n(f)$. If $x\in X^n$ is closed and $fx=d_Yy$, then $(-y,x)$ is a cone cycle of degree $n-1$. Writing it as $d_C(w,t)$ yields $x=-d_Xt$, proving injectivity. Thus $C(f)$ is acyclic exactly when every $H^n(f)$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 09KW, lemma-acyclic; direct cycle computation for the cone and cohomology defined in the statement, spelling out the cone long-exact-sequence criterion without an uncited boundary comparison.

proof.text: The zero module is acyclic. Step 6 shows that acyclicity is invariant under every isomorphism of $K_A$ and under every positive or negative shift; hence the full subcategory $\mathcal E$ is strictly full and shift-closed. If $X\to Y\to Z\to X[1]$ is distinguished with $X,Z$ acyclic, choose a cone normal form $T_f$; its corresponding source and cone are acyclic by isomorphism invariance. Step 7 implies that $H^n(f)$ is an isomorphism for every $n$, and its source cohomology is zero, so its target cohomology is zero as well. Thus $Y$ is acyclic. These are exactly the closure conditions of [def-weil-triangulated-subcategory], so $\mathcal E$ is a strictly full triangulated subcategory of the triangulated category proved in step 5.

source.place: Tag 09KW, lemma-acyclic; closure conditions in derived.tex Tag 05QM, definition-triangulated-subcategory.

proof.text: For a morphism $u$ choose a chain-map representative $f$. If all $H^n(u)$ are isomorphisms, step 7 makes $C(f)$ acyclic, and $T_f$ is the distinguished triangle witnessing $u\in W_{\mathcal E}$. Conversely, a distinguished triangle witnessing $u\in W_{\mathcal E}$ is isomorphic to some $T_f$. Its cone is acyclic by step 6, so step 7 makes every $H^n(f)$ invertible. The first square of that triangle isomorphism expresses $H^n(u)$ as $H^n(f)$ composed on either side with isomorphisms. Thus every $H^n(u)$ is invertible. This proves precisely the equality of classes in the statement. All constructions above are finite sums, shifts, quotients of Hom groups and explicit $A$-linear maps in the fixed universes; no boundedness or commutativity has been used.
